title: UX review
summary: Review a UI against Nielsen’s 10 usability heuristics.

overview.purpose: Before you finish a UI, review it against these 10 usability heuristics.
overview.when: A screen is built and you need to name what fails, where, and the fix.
takeaways: Name the screen, the problem, and the fix
Say what failed and how to fix it

sections.title: Ten heuristics
sections.intro: It looks X, so do Y. For each one that fails, name the screen, the problem, and the fix.

items.title: Visibility of system status
items.fix: It looks frozen, so show progress or a state change within 1 second.

items.title: Match between system and the real world
items.fix: It sounds like the system, so use the user’s words and a familiar order.

items.title: User control and freedom
items.fix: It feels like a trap, so add Undo, Back, or Cancel.

items.title: Consistency and standards
items.fix: It acts differently each time, so use the same pattern and label everywhere.

items.title: Error prevention
items.fix: It’s easy to get wrong, so add limits, good defaults, and confirmation for risky actions.

items.title: Recognition rather than recall
items.fix: It makes me remember, so keep options and context visible.

items.title: Flexibility and efficiency of use
items.fix: It’s slow for experts, so add shortcuts without hiding the basics.

items.title: Aesthetic and minimalist design
items.fix: It’s noisy, so remove anything that doesn’t help the task.

items.title: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
items.fix: The error is vague, so say what happened and how to fix it in plain words.

items.title: Help and documentation
items.fix: I’m stuck, so give short help in context, right where it’s needed.
